title: High Molecular Weight DNA Extraction from Recalcitrant Plant Species for Third Generation Sequencing
author: Rachael Workman
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.4vbgw2n
materials: Carefully mix for 00:20:00 at Room temperature . Verify that the fluid is continuously mixing and that the Nanobind disk remains submerged in the binding solution throughout the binding process for efficient recovery of DNA. ● Mixing can be performed by inverting the tubes and placing them cap-side downon a HulaMixer (Thermo Fisher) or similar device. ● If a HulaMixer in not available, manually mix the tubes by inversion (e.g., 5X inversions every 00:02:00 ) to facilitate binding. ● A tube rotator is not recommended, as low reaction volume precludes adequate mixing during end over end rotation.

steps.title: Grind tissue and homogenize
steps.instruction: Grind 1 g fresh or snap‑frozen plant tissue into a fine powder in liquid nitrogen using a mortar and pestle. Transfer the powder to a capped 250 mL bottle containing 10 mL NIB. Cap the bottle and place it on an end‑over‑end mixer (or on a shaker at 150 rpm, or on a stir plate with a stir bar) rotating at maximum speed for 15 min (00:15:00) at 4 °C.

steps.title: Filter homogenate and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Gravity‑filter the homogenate through five layers of Miracloth into a 50 mL conical tube using a funnel. Cap the tube and centrifuge at 4 °C for 20 min (00:20:00). Centrifugation speed should be adjusted to genome size (larger genomes such as redwood (30 Gb) require higher speed, walnut (1 Gb) lower speed, maize (2.5 Gb) intermediate).

steps.title: Wash nuclei pellet
steps.instruction: Decant the supernatant, add 1 mL cold NIB to the pellet, and resuspend the pellet with a paint‑brush pre‑soaked in NIB (pipetting with wide‑bore tips works for some species such as maize, but many species require the brush because the pellet is too sticky).

steps.title: Adjust volume and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Transfer the 1 mL nuclei suspension to a 15 mL conical tube, bring the volume up to 15 mL with ice‑cold NIB, and centrifuge at 4 °C for 10 min (00:10:00).

steps.title: Assess supernatant and repeat wash
steps.instruction: If the supernatant after centrifugation is clear, decant it and keep the pellet for the next step. If coloration remains, discard the supernatant, resuspend the nuclei pellet in NIB, bring the volume to 10–15 mL, and repeat this wash up to 3–5 times for conifer tissue; for maize additional washes are usually unnecessary.

steps.title: Resuspend nuclei in HB
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant and resuspend the nuclei pellet in 1 mL 1X HB (homogenization buffer).

steps.title: Choose storage or lysis
steps.instruction: Decide whether to snap‑freeze the nuclei or proceed directly to lysis.

steps.title: Snap‑freeze nuclei
steps.instruction: Spin the nuclei suspension in a 1.5 mL tube at the temperature indicated (‑) for 5 min (00:05:00), discard the supernatant, snap‑freeze the pellet in liquid nitrogen, and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Proceed to lysis
steps.instruction: Spin the nuclei suspension in a 1.5 mL tube at the temperature indicated (‑) for 5 min (00:05:00), discard the supernatant, and continue to the lysis steps.

steps.title: Add Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Resuspend the isolated nuclei with 30 µL Proteinase K, vortex on high until fully resuspended, and spin the tube on a mini‑centrifuge for 2 s (00:00:02) to remove liquid from the cap.

steps.title: Optional RNA removal
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL RNase A, pulse‑vortex 5 times, spin 2 s (00:00:02) to remove liquid, and incubate at room temperature for 3 min (00:03:00). Skip this step if RNA removal is not required.

steps.title: Add Lysis Buffer PL1
steps.instruction: Add 80 µL Buffer PL1, pulse‑vortex 10 times, spin 2 s (00:00:02) to remove liquid. If the mixture appears inhomogeneous, vortex continuously on high for 10 s (00:00:10) until it is cloudy, viscous, and homogeneous.

steps.title: Incubate for lysis
steps.instruction: Incubate on a ThermoMixer at 55 °C, 900 rpm for 30 min (00:30:00). Pulse‑vortex 5 times during incubation and invert the tube 5 times every 5 min (00:05:00). If a ThermoMixer is unavailable, use a dry‑bath or water bath at 55 °C and invert manually. Extend incubation up to 2 h (02:00:00) if lysis is incomplete.

steps.title: Clarify lysate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate at room temperature for 5 min (00:05:00).

steps.title: Transfer supernatant to LoBind tube
steps.instruction: Transfer the cleared supernatant to a new 1.5 mL Protein LoBind microcentrifuge tube using a wide‑bore pipette, handling gently to avoid shearing.

steps.title: Bind DNA to Nanobind disk
steps.instruction: Add a Nanobind disk to the supernatant, then add an equal (1×) volume of isopropanol (adjust proportionally if supernatant >150 µL). The disk must be added before the isopropanol.

steps.title: Magnetic capture and first washes
steps.instruction: Place the tube on a magnetic rack, allow the disk to collect, discard the supernatant without touching the disk, add 500 µL Buffer PW1, invert‑mix 4 times, return the tube to the magnet, and discard the wash buffer. Repeat this wash a second time.

steps.title: Remove residual wash buffer
steps.instruction: Spin the tube on a mini‑centrifuge for 2 s (00:00:02) and remove any residual liquid from the cap. If the Nanobind disk blocks the tube bottom, gently push it aside with the tip of a pipette.

steps.title: Repeat PW1 wash until dry
steps.instruction: Repeat the Buffer PW1 wash (step 9) until no residual wash buffer remains on the disk or tube walls; the tube should appear dry.

steps.title: Elute DNA
steps.instruction: Add 50–200 µL Buffer EB, spin 2 s (00:00:02), incubate at room temperature for 10 min (00:10:00), ensuring the entire Nanobind disk is fully immersed. Elution volume may be adjusted to downstream requirements; the disk may be gently compressed with a pipette tip if needed.

steps.title: Collect eluate
steps.instruction: Transfer the eluate to a fresh 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube using a wide‑bore pipette, spin 5 s (00:00:05), and transfer any remaining liquid. Repeat if necessary. Using a wide‑bore tip helps preserve DNA fragments of 50–300 kb or longer.

steps.title: Assess DNA quality
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration and purity using a NanoDrop spectrophotometer and a Qubit fluorometer.
